PullRequest.Title: Agents window: add connected chat and side-panel tabs
PullRequest.Body:
This brings connected tabs to the Agents window's chat and side-panel tab bars, so the selected tab joins its content surface instead of appearing as a separate pill. ### Changes - Both tab bars follow `workbench.experimental.modernUIEditorTabStyle`: connected by default, with pill mode retained. Changes apply immediately, independently of the broader Modern UI setting. - Reuse the shared connected-tab geometry and clipping behavior while matching chat tabs to the active/inactive session background. - Preserve compact sizing, keyboard navigation, close actions, status indicators, inline renaming, and high-contrast focus boundaries. - Exclude the Add Tab toolbar from editor-tab measurement so the docked Details panel cannot overlap the tab strip. - Remove the old divider beneath connected chat tabs and correctly anchor the right-overflow mask. - Add regression coverage and themed fixtures, and update the tab-style documentation. ### Validation - `npm run gulp compile-client` - passed with zero compilation errors. - 317 focused tests passed across chat tabs/groups, workbench layout, editor contributions, editor tabs, and Modern UI. - ESLint, CSS lint, layer checks, and `git diff --check` passed. - The reported Search-hover/Details overlap was reproduced and verified fixed in a running Code OSS Agents window. - Captured the 16 production-component screenshots below from commit `352dd22de51`. Capture assertions checked tab height, surface colors, connected/pill geometry, Add Tab visibility, icon fonts, and the right-clipping mask position. **Build environment limitation:** the broader `npm run compile-client` task, which also builds extensions/media, was blocked by the missing `@vscode/markdown-editor` dependency. Restoring that unchanged extension's dependencies failed with npm `E401`. The core client compilation and focused tests above passed. ### How to test 1. Open the Agents window with the tab style set to `connected`. Open multiple chats and several side-panel tabs, including Changes, Browser, and Search. 2. Hover, switch, close, and rename tabs; open the Add Tab menu and toggle Details. The Details pane should start below the tab strip. 3. Resize and scroll overflowing chat/editor tabs. Check the selected tab's shoulders and clipped edges. 4. Switch between `connected` and `pill`, default/compact tab height, and light/dark/high-contrast themes. ### Screenshot proof These are production component fixtures with deterministic sample data, captured on macOS at 2x resolution. Images are pinned to an immutable evidence commit in my fork; screenshot binaries are **not** included in this PR's code diff. Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed event handlers, synchronous Scrollable event propagation, write-before-read ordering, exact geometry/style operations, and overflow trigger are all directly traced in repository code. Exact frame cost varies by machine and DOM size, but the repeated synchronous-layout mechanism is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: browser style resolution and layout work from class/style mutations, three getBoundingClientRect calls, clientWidth, and two getComputedStyle calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The forced style/layout work repeats for every horizontal scroll event and can run twice per movement through the native-scroll and ScrollableElement callbacks; active-tab lookup also grows with the number of chat tabs.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased scrolling latency and dropped frames while horizontally scrolling an overflowing chat tab strip
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The native scroll listener only synchronized scrollLeft into ScrollableElement, and the ScrollableElement listener only copied its position back to the DOM; neither path measured tab geometry or resolved styles.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Both scroll synchronization handlers now call _updateConnectedTabClipping, which clears clipping classes/styles, finds the active tab, then immediately reads three DOM rectangles, clientWidth, and two computed styles before writing clipping state.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 204 newly invokes _updateConnectedTabClipping from the native scroll event; the same diff also invokes it from ScrollableElement.onScroll and adds the synchronous geometry/style reads in that routine.
Findings.Title: Cache clipping geometry off the scroll path
Findings.Impact: With enough chats to overflow the strip, wheel, trackpad, or drag scrolling places synchronous layout/style work on every movement. setScrollPositionNow fires ScrollableElement.onScroll synchronously when the position changes, so a native scroll can execute the routine once from that callback and again when the native handler resumes, making visible tab scrolling prone to jank.
Findings.Evidence: The added call at line 204 is inside the native SCROLL listener. That listener first calls ScrollableElement.setScrollPosition; Scrollable.setScrollPositionNow synchronously calls _setState, which fires onScroll when scrollLeft changes, reaching the second added call at line 211. _updateConnectedTabClipping starts by mutating classes/styles via clearConnectedTabClipping, then reads _tabsContainer, active fill, and scrollbar getBoundingClientRect(), clientWidth, and two getComputedStyle values. The existing editor-tab implementation avoids this by computing IConnectedTabBounds during layout and having its scroll callback perform only updateConnectedTabClipping arithmetic/class toggles.
Findings.Recommendation: Compute and cache IConnectedTabBounds and the radii when tabs are rebuilt, the active tab changes, or the ResizeObserver fires, as MultiEditorTabsControl does. On scroll, update clipping from the cached bounds and current scrollLeft through one synchronization path (or coalesce to one animation-frame update).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The newly activated condition, default Agents configuration, resize-to-layout call path, per-tab operations, and unbounded Browser-tab cardinality are directly established in code. Exact frame impact depends on tab count and platform style/layout cost, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread computed-style queries, canvas text measurement/cache lookups, DOM queries, CSS custom-property writes, and offsetWidth layout reads for every tab
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(open side-panel editor tabs) on each animation-frame layout while the Agents window or its Details/editor split is resized; Browser tabs use unique IDs, so this collection can realistically grow beyond the built-in Changes/Search/Files tabs.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased resize latency and dropped frames when resizing an Agents window or dragging its editor/detail sash with many open tabs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Agents windows did not satisfy the old `.modern-ui.modern-ui-connected-editor-tabs` condition and had a read-only pill-style override, so layoutConnectedTabLabels(false) skipped per-tab computed styles, text metrics, decoration metrics, and offsetWidth reads.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The broadened `.modern-ui-tabs.modern-ui-connected-editor-tabs` condition makes connected true for the Agents side-panel tab bar by default. Every scheduled doLayout then runs layoutConnectedTabLabels(true), which recomputes each tab's intrinsic minimum metrics before reading every tab's offsetWidth.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 2069 replaces the Modern-UI-only ancestor check with the Agents-compatible modern-ui-tabs check; together with the diff's removal of the Agents pill override and new connected-style contribution, this newly activates the expensive connected-label branch for every Agents side-panel layout.
Findings.Title: Cache connected-label metrics across resize layouts
Findings.Impact: During continuous resize, the control schedules one layout per animation frame and repeats up to several getComputedStyle calls per tab plus width reads on the UI thread. With many file/browser/search editors open in the Agents side panel, this consumes the frame budget and makes sash or window resizing visibly stutter.
Findings.Evidence: SinglePaneMainEditorPart sets useModernUITabs and supplies an Add Tab menu; NewBrowserTabAction creates a fresh UUID-backed editor each time. EditorGroupView.layout calls titleControl.layout for every group resize, and MultiEditorTabsControl schedules doLayout on the next frame. The changed condition at line 2069 now enters layoutConnectedTabLabels(true), whose per-tab body queries label nodes, reads getComputedStyle for the tab/name/ellipsis/suffix/badge, writes minimum-width properties, then reads offsetWidth for every measured tab. The text-width LRU does not avoid the computed-style reads or offsetWidth pass.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache each tab's intrinsic minimum width and font/decorative metrics, invalidating only when that tab's label, decorations, theme/font, or relevant editor options change. Width-only resize layouts should reuse those minima and perform only the current-width/narrow-state work needed for the new viewport.

Scenarios.Scenario: Horizontally scroll an overflowing connected chat-tab strip in the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each native or ScrollableElement scroll update synchronously reaches clipping-state calculation before the next paint; the geometry/style reads are therefore on the interaction critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous browser style resolution and layout through class/style writes followed by getBoundingClientRect, clientWidth, and getComputedStyle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two full clipping measurements per scroll movement, each with three rectangle reads, one clientWidth read, two computed-style reads, and an O(chat tabs) active-tab scan
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The two listeners only synchronized scroll positions; they performed no clipping geometry or style measurements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks handling of the current scroll update and competes directly with the next paint, causing scroll jank.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll-event frequency and the number of chat tabs. A realistic overflow fixture uses 5-6 long-titled chats; active-tab lookup scans the effective tab collection once per clipping update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is serialized on the renderer main thread. A native scroll updates ScrollableElement synchronously, so its onScroll callback can run before the native listener resumes, producing two clipping updates for one movement rather than coalescing at animation-frame granularity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No clipping geometry or computed radii are cached. The active tab, three rectangles, client width, and two computed-style values are recomputed on each call; cold and warm paths are equivalent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: synchronous event propagation, duplicate reachability, write-before-read ordering, and all DOM operations are directly visible in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout duration depends on platform, theme, tab DOM size, and browser state, but trackpad/wheel events are frequent and overflow with several chats is explicitly supported.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity synchronous UI regression; clipping geometry should be cached outside the scroll path and updates coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize the Agents window or drag the editor/Details split with connected side-panel tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: EditorGroupView forwards each size change to the title control; MultiEditorTabsControl coalesces to one doLayout per animation frame, but connected-label metric work must complete on the UI thread before that frame's tab layout and paint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Per-tab computed-style resolution, label-node queries, optional canvas text measurement, CSS property writes, and offsetWidth layout reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several style reads plus one width read per non-compact tab, once per animation-frame layout during continuous resize
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agents used pill tabs and failed the old Modern-UI-only connected condition, so this side-panel path skipped intrinsic text/style and offsetWidth measurement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Consumes resize-frame budget before tab rendering can settle, leading to sash/window resize stutter as tab count grows.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is every open editor tab in the Agents side-panel group. Built-in tabs are few, but Browser creates a fresh UUID-backed editor each time and files/search editors can increase the collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One coalesced tab layout per animation frame, serialized on the renderer main thread; there is no worker or limiter beyond frame coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Canvas text widths have a 256-entry LRU, but every frame still reads computed styles to construct cache keys. The per-tab minimumWidths map is recreated each layout, CSS minima are rewritten, and offsetWidth is reread for every tab; width-independent intrinsic metrics are not retained per tab.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default connected state, broadened ancestor condition, resize call path, frame scheduling, and per-tab operations are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact tab count at which frames drop depends on hardware and theme/style complexity, but the Agents editor group can realistically accumulate many uniquely identified Browser and file tabs.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated layout work; cache intrinsic tab metrics and invalidate them only for content/style changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an Agents window, add auxiliary containers, or toggle the connected/pill tab-style setting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At startup the BlockStartup contribution toggles one class per existing container. A setting change toggles classes, performs one main layout, then one layout per auxiliary window; these operations are synchronous but initiated by a rare explicit setting change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Workbench and auxiliary-window layout after a tab-style class change
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One main layout plus one layout per auxiliary window per explicit setting change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agents did not independently apply this setting or trigger these layouts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The setting UI waits for synchronous relayout, but the event is rare and container count is small.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workbench containers/windows, normally one main container and a small bounded set of auxiliary windows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Layouts are invoked serially, once per affected container/window; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls are reached by the changed code.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The setting is read once per container application. There is no cache, but the work is constant per container and only repeats on the specific setting change or container addition.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Auxiliary-window count varies, but realistic counts are small and the trigger is user-driven rather than hot.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: bounded work on a rare configuration event is appropriate for immediate visual application.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, activate, resize, or change visibility of connected chat tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat collection changes rebuild tab DOM and active-tab changes update classes, scroll dimensions, reveal the selected tab, and compute clipping. ResizeObserver callbacks perform the same dimension/reveal work before the resulting paint; no remote service call is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM creation/rebuild, scroll dimension reads, scrollIntoView, and connected clipping geometry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass over all chats per collection rebuild or active-chat update; one clipping calculation per reveal/resize, excluding separately analyzed scroll duplication
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Tab creation and active-state scans already existed; the diff adds connected decoration and clipping calculations and moves dimension refresh into active updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the selected chat/tab presentation settles, but outside continuous scrolling these events are discrete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats in the active session; rebuild is O(chats), active selection scans/updates the same collection, and resize is observer-coalesced by the browser.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer-main-thread DOM work; ResizeObserver delivery is browser scheduled. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tab DOM is deliberately rebuilt when the chat collection changes. Active/reveal geometry is not cached, which contributes to the separately reported scroll-path issue, but collection and active-chat updates themselves are lower-frequency.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for code path; lower concern for user-visible cost outside scrolling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions with very large chat counts are possible but typical activation/rebuild frequency is low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the scroll-path report: discrete active/rebuild/resize costs are bounded and necessary for the connected presentation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all 19 changed files and all paginated diff content. Reported two UI-thread regressions: duplicate forced clipping measurements on chat-tab scrolling, and repeated per-tab connected-label metric work newly activated for Agents side-panel resize layouts. Checked startup/configuration relayout, tab lifecycle, CSS/theme expansion, helper extraction, tests, and expensive external boundaries; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is introduced.
